extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and mentors for NIH K08 (Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award) and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for evaluating a mentored clinical scientist (K08) career development grant application, covering candidate qualifications, career development plan, research plan, mentorship, environment, and required compliance items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: Based upon the evaluation of scientific and technical merit, this application received an Overall Impact/Priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by individual reviewers, are not discussed specifically at the review meeting, and are not calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. Use the overall impact score to reflect likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, prior training, productivity, publications, clinical training, awards, and potential to become an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate strengths such as excellent prior research training, relevant publications, awards, and clinical competence. Note weaknesses such as lack of significant first-author publications during recent training. Consider how the candidate's background and demonstrated productivity support their proposed career trajectory and ability to complete the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals & Objectives / Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the career development plan including didactic coursework, technical training, mentorship structure, grant-writing and mentoring training, milestones, timeline, and explicit plans to transition from K-award to R01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong plans include relevant coursework (immunology, biostatistics, computing, gene expression, clinical practices), mentorship and grant-writing training, protected research time, milestones (presentations, manuscripts, R01 submission), and explicit metrics for measuring success. Weaknesses include insufficient protected time (concern that 80% in years 1-2 may not be enough). Ensure plans for mentoring and meeting presentations, manuscript submissions, and R01/other funding applications are clear and time-lined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the scientific rationale, significance, specific aims, experimental design, feasibility, preliminary data, integration with career development, and potential for impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether aims are well-justified, integrated with the career plan, and feasible given available methods and cohorts. Consider sample size and power calculations, whether individual aims are appropriately related (concern if Aim 3 is tangential), availability/validation of key assays (e.g., IPDA), and whether inclusion criteria (e.g., viral load <200 c/mL) may introduce heterogeneity. Look for alternative plans addressing sample or cell-number limitations and clear statistical plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the qualifications, complementary expertise, commitment, and letters of support from mentors/co-mentors/collaborators and the clarity of their roles in training the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong mentoring teams provide detailed letters specifying expectations and contributions, complementary expertise pertinent to both the career development and research plan, and clear access to technical methods and clinical cohorts. Weaknesses include insufficiently detailed or non-independent mentoring plans. Consider whether mentors will provide hands-on training, resources, and guidance for transitioning to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment / Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the research environment, institutional resources, cohort access, and institutional assurances (appointments, protected time) that support the candidate's success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for strong institutional letters of support, guaranteed appointments, access to clinical cohorts and core facilities, adequate funding in the mentor's lab, and explicit assurances of protected research time. Institutional commitment is a critical factor for the feasibility of the career development plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance / Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposed research addresses an important problem or critical barrier to progress in the field and the potential to improve public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the project addresses clinically significant populations (e.g., suboptimal immune responders on ART) and whether results could inform therapeutics or change clinical practice. Emphasize the potential impact on morbidity and mortality for high-risk populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the application challenges current paradigms or employs novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies (e.g., use of new assays such as the intact proviral DNA assay (IPDA)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovative aspects may include novel hypotheses, duplex-droplet digital PCR assays that discriminate intact vs defective proviruses, or integration of novel induction assays. Review whether claimed innovations are sufficiently supported and whether method details or validation are available to judge novelty and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach / Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the robustness of experimental design, methods (e.g., IPDA, quantitative viral induction assays), controls, sample and tissue sources (blood, lymph node), statistical analyses, power calculations, and contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key considerations include feasibility of assays with available cell numbers, appropriateness of controls and matching (age, nadir CD4, sex, race, co-infections), power to detect hypothesized effects (concern about small patient samples for IL7/IL15), alternative approaches if sample limitations arise, and availability of preliminary data demonstrating assay performance. Explicit validation data for key assays strengthens the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and sufficiency of preliminary data to support feasibility of key assays and the overall experimental plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong applications provide preliminary results demonstrating assay feasibility, sample availability, and expected effect sizes. Lack of validation data for critical assays (e.g., IPDA discrimination of intact vs defective proviruses) is a notable weakness and should be addressed or justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Size / Statistical Power and Cohort Characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of proposed sample sizes, power calculations, and clear description of cohorts and numbers of eligible participants (e.g., numbers of suboptimal immune responders in named cohorts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for explicit counts/estimates of available subjects, justification that sample sizes are sufficient to address aims, and attention to inclusion criteria that may introduce heterogeneity (e.g., viral load thresholds). If cohort numbers are not stated or sample sizes for interventions (IL7/IL15) are limited, note as a weakness and consider feasibility and power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay Validation (e.g., IPDA validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation and demonstrated ability of critical assays (such as the intact proviral DNA assay) to distinguish intended targets (intact vs defective proviruses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should present data showing assay discrimination ability and limitations. If referenced methods are in-press or unpublished, reviewers may judge appropriateness conservatively and request validation data or alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected Research Time
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of protected research effort proposed for the candidate (e.g., 80% protected time) and whether it is sufficient to accomplish the career development and research goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposed percent effort is realistic for accomplishing aims within the award period. Reviewers may express concern if early years' protected time seems insufficient to establish the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support / Mentor Letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Content and strength of mentor and institutional letters describing commitments, expectations, resources to be provided, and evidence of sponsor support (e.g., guaranteed appointment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong, detailed letters that spell out mentor responsibilities, available resources, and institutional commitments bolster the application. Letters from collaborators providing access to cohorts or critical resources are important. Lack of independent or external letters may be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestones, Timeline, and Plans for Transition to Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear milestones and timeline for training activities, presentations, manuscripts, grant submissions (e.g., plan to apply for R01 during year 4) and other metrics for measuring career development success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should include a realistic timeline for achieving training goals and for transitioning to independent funding, with specific deliverables (manuscripts, R01 submission targets) and interim milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of protections for human subjects, including adherence to NIH policies and appropriate documentation (Code 10 NOT APPLICABLE when no human subjects involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects involving human subjects must conform to NIH policies; reviewers will check protocol protections, consent, and compliance. If code 10 is assigned, human subjects issues are not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to include a data and safety monitoring plan where applicable (NOT APPLICABLE for some training grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical trials or studies with safety concerns need an appropriate monitoring plan. For K-awards that do not involve interventional trials, this may be N/A but should be addressed if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with NIH policies on humane care and use of laboratory animals (Code 10 NOT APPLICABLE if no live vertebrate animals involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If vertebrate animals are used, applicants must provide appropriate protocols and compliance information in accordance with NIH/OLAW policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard Safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biological hazard issues and whether plans for handling biohazardous materials are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers comment whether biohazard handling and containment plans are acceptable for the proposed work. Marked as 'ACCEPTABLE' when plans are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of the plan for RCR training including subject matter, format, faculty participation, duration and frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should cover conflict of interest, human subjects policies, mentor/mentee responsibilities, collaborative research, data management, misconduct policies, authorship, and contemporary ethical issues. Specify format (face-to-face discussions, colloquia), faculty involvement, and contact hours (e.g., 8 contact hours spread over award period plus informal interactions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data Sharing, Model Organisms, GDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to share data, model organisms, and genomic data where applicable (e.g., 'ACCEPTABLE' or 'NOT APPLICABLE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable (large grants, genomics), data sharing plans should conform to NIH policies. For K-awards these sections may be 'NOT APPLICABLE' or 'ACCEPTABLE' depending on scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to authenticate key biological/chemical resources used in the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applicants address how they will validate cell lines, reagents, and other critical resources to prevent misidentification or contamination; reviewers will note acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the requested budget and period of support for appropriateness and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may recommend budget as requested or propose adjustments; institute grants management will calculate final costs if award is planned. Justify requested resources and protected time in the application.
